subject.title: [Bug]: childless codex-native subagent stuck initializing can exhaust unified exec capacity

question: What recovery policy should OpenClaw use when a childless Codex-native subagent remains `pendingInit` or `running` without progress long enough to threaten Codex execution capacity?
rationale: The current 30-minute policy is intentional and documented, but changing it can prematurely terminalize valid slow native subagents; the source supports the bug impact but does not determine the product-safe cutoff or recovery mechanism.

options.title: Add health-based early recovery
options.body: Use Codex-native status or transcript health signals to warn, audit, or mark only clearly stalled childless mirrors before the 30-minute fallback.

options.title: Shorten the fixed grace
options.body: Reduce the childless Codex-native grace for all mirrors, accepting the risk that slow-but-valid native subagents may be marked lost earlier.

options.title: Diagnostics only first
options.body: Keep the 30-minute fallback and add status, audit, and version diagnostics so maintainers can gather live evidence before changing terminalization policy.

recommendation.title: Add health-based early recovery
recommendation.body: Use Codex-native status or transcript health signals to warn, audit, or mark only clearly stalled childless mirrors before the 30-minute fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent merged work on both childless Codex-native task recovery and blocked-spawn terminalization, which are the closest current ownership signals for this policy choice.
